slots.title: Core wholesale prices up 0.7% in September
slots.body:
Core PPI (prices suppliers charge, minus food and energy) came in at +0.7% for September.

Economists had looked for +0.3%; the prior month was +0.2%.

Headline producer prices rose +1.3% on the month versus a +0.5% estimate.

Year over year, PPI ran at +6.3% versus +5.3% expected.

Coverage tied the print to another uptick in inflation gauges after this week’s consumer price data.

Which part of the supply chain do you watch first when PPI runs hot?

slots.title: September retail sales miss headline, beat ex autos
slots.body:
September retail sales (total spending at stores, online, and restaurants) rose +0.1% from August.

The consensus was +0.3%; August’s revision context in the data was +1.2% prior month for headline sales.

Strip out autos and the month-over-month gain was +0.9% versus +0.5% expected.

Year over year, retail sales were up +6.3% versus +5.2% expected.

Ex gas and autos, the month-over-month change matched expectations at +0.2%.

When headline sales lag but ex-auto sales beat, how do you read consumer demand?

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 15, 2026
slots.body:
The Dow led the major U.S. indexes on Oct. 15, closing at 52,177.69 (+556.21 pts, +1.1%).
The Russell 2000 rose +1.4% to 2,767.27.
The S&P 500 added +0.3% to 7,744.09, and the Nasdaq Composite edged +0.1% to 26,713.03 — a wide gap between blue-chip and growth benchmarks that matched commentary about rotation after pressure on AI-linked shares.

At 12:30 p.m.
ET, September retail sales rose 0.1% month over month versus a 0.3% consensus, slowing from August’s 1.2%.
Excluding autos, sales rose 0.9% vs 0.5% expected.
Retail sales were up 6.3% year over year vs 5.2% expected.
The NY Empire State manufacturing index printed 25.5 vs 10.3 expected.

Producer prices for September rose 1.3% MoM (est. 0.5%) with core PPI up 0.7% MoM (est. 0.3%).
PPI was up 6.3% YoY vs 5.3% est.
Jobless claims: 199K initial (est. 200K), 1710K continuing, four-week average 198.5K.
Atlanta Fed GDPNow for Q3 held at 3.6%.

On the Nasdaq sector map, Financial Services averaged +2.1%, Technology +1.9%, Industrials +1.3%, and Communication Services +1.4%.
Consumer Defensive lagged at -1.9%, Utilities -0.8%, Basic Materials -0.6%, and Energy -0.7%.

Earnings drove several large financial moves.
Marsh & McLennan ($MRSH) closed +4.6% at 186.54 on EPS $2.03 vs $1.97 est and revenue above forecast.
Bank of New York Mellon ($BNY) rose +3.2% to 142.09 after EPS $2.37 vs $2.27 est. U.S. Bancorp ($USB) gained +2.0% to 57.39; PNC ($PNC) reported EPS $5.09 vs $4.91 est but finished -0.4% at 214.94.
Charles Schwab ($SCHW) beat on EPS ($1.69 vs $1.65) yet closed -2.7% at 94.16.

Outside banks, Salesforce ($CRM) rose +4.6% to 246.74.
Eli Lilly ($LLY) closed +3.5% at 1,251.61.
UnitedHealth ($UNH) added +2.8% to 406.67.
Visa ($V) was +2.1% at 399.75, near its 403.21 52-week high.
NVIDIA ($NVDA) fell -1.8% to 217.23 on elevated volume; Intel ($INTC) was -2.8% to 95.37.
Prologis ($PLD) reported EPS $1.60 vs $0.777 est and revenue ~$2.39B vs ~$2.18B est but the stock still closed -2.7% at 126.94.

Energy megacaps softened: Exxon Mobil ($XOM) -1.3% to 174.64, Chevron ($CVX) -1.2% to 219.39, while the USO oil ETF rose +2.4% to 157.31.
Brent crude in the cross-asset feed was -0.5% at 105.42.

Gold futures (GC) settled +0.7% at 4,200.10.
Bitcoin was +0.6% at 82,011.77.
The UUP dollar proxy was -0.4% at 29.00.
The VIX fell -2.4% to 16.46.

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-10-13) showed the 10-year at 5.2% and the 2s10s spread at 0.42 percentage points.

Overseas indexes in the feed closed higher ahead of or alongside the U.S. move: Nikkei 225 +1.7% to 65,550.68, FTSE 100 +1.1%, Hang Seng +1.3%.
